summary: Buck Hill, Alger County MI: 100-ft steel tower; a 1935 cabin built by CCC-camp laborers; now hosts a state police repeater. No build date or access info found.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with a cabin on top
facts.status_note: Cabin floor has failed, though the steel is in good shape

staffing.status: two men worked the lookout for six summers before 1935; the NHLR says David O. Evans worked there in the mid-1950s

events.note: in an October 1935 report, two men had worked here for six summers, living in a shack left from a logging camp
new log cabin ordered after the old building reached an almost uninhabitable stage; built by laborers from the state CCC camp at Cusino
1943-44 state report: portable tower cabin built from salvaged material placed at the tower
NHLR says David O. Evans worked here in the mid-1950s; exact year not given

notes_for_editor: No build date found; the 1935 item already describes an existing tower. Access and visiting rules were not found, so the story says so and the facts block omits access. The NHLR lists the cooperator as 'Painted Rocks National Lakeshore', which I suspect means Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore; not verified and not in the story. The easternuslookouts Alger county page says CCC crews built eight new towers in 1937-38 and that one was at 'the Alger site'; I could not tie that to this tower, so it is not used. The 1935 and 1943-44 items are quoted through the easternuslookouts page, not the original newspaper or report. The NHLR mid-1950s staffing date is approximate, so the event year 1955 is a placeholder.
